page.title: Hybrid Event Production Timeline Guide
page.description: A week-by-week breakdown of hybrid event production, from venue lock to rehearsal, with staffing, workstreams and deliverables mapped to real lead times.
page.h1: How long does hybrid event production take?
page.definition: Hybrid event production is the end-to-end process of planning, staffing, rehearsing and delivering an event that runs simultaneously for an in-room audience and a live online stream, with a single run of show owned by one producer.
page.quick_answer: Start six to eight weeks out for a conference or summit; three to four weeks for a webinar. Lock venue AV and platform first, then build the run of show, assign workstream owners and schedule one full rehearsal two to five days before go-live.

sections.h2: How far in advance should I start planning a hybrid event?

blocks.p: A hybrid conference or summit needs six to eight weeks of management; a webinar needs three to four weeks. The venue AV contract and the streaming platform must be locked before the agenda is final, because both dictate what is possible on the day.

ul: Week one: intake, brief, platform and venue AV confirmed
Weeks two to four: speaker confirmations, slide templates, registration open
Weeks four to six: run of show drafted, moderator briefed, backup stream configured
Week six to eight: full rehearsal, technical check, go-live

sections.h2: What are the key milestones in a hybrid production timeline?

blocks.p: Seven steps each have an owner, an output and an approval gate, moving from intake through publishing to reporting. The platform is not the production; someone must own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready.

ol: Intake: scope, dates, budget, platform choice
Brief: audience outcomes, format, speaker list
Production: run of show, lower thirds, branded slides
Review: internal stakeholder sign-off on flow
Approval: final run of show locked
Publishing: live stream, registration, replay page

sections.h2: Which workstreams need owners and when do they start?

blocks.p: Eight workstreams run in parallel, each with one named owner. Starting them on the right week prevents bottlenecks when the agenda shifts.

sections.h2: What staffing does a hybrid event need compared to a webinar?

blocks.p: One producer can run a simple webinar; summits and hybrid events need a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator. The crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream are production purchases separate from the platform licence.

ul: Show caller: owns timing, cues, run of show changes live
Speaker manager: green room, tech checks, slide uploads
Moderator: live Q&A, chat, audience polls
Platform operator: stream health, backup encoder, recording
Camera operator: in-room feeds, switcher coordination

sections.h2: When should rehearsals and technical checks happen?

blocks.p: One full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go-live, plus a technical check sixty minutes before doors open. A repeat format can move faster, but the rehearsal window protects against platform updates and speaker environment changes.

ul: Full rehearsal: all speakers, show caller, platform operator, moderator
Technical check: audio, video, backup stream, lower thirds, polls
Speaker environment test: lighting, microphone, internet, screen share
Run-of-show walkthrough: timing, transitions, emergency cues

sections.h2: What deliverables should be ready before go-live?

blocks.p: The production package includes run of show, speaker brief and rehearsal, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and clips. Send the replay within twenty-four to forty-eight hours while attendees still remember the event.

ul: Final run of show with timecodes and owner column
Speaker brief deck with platform instructions and backup contacts
Branded slide master and lower-third graphics package
Configured backup stream on secondary encoder
Edited recording and highlight clips for distribution

faq.q: Can I compress a hybrid summit into four weeks?
faq.a: Only if the format is a repeat, the platform and venue AV are already contracted, and speakers have pre-recorded segments. New agendas, new speakers or new venues need the full six to eight weeks to absorb scope changes without cutting rehearsal time.

faq.q: Who owns the run of show on the day?
faq.a: The show caller owns the run of show live. They call cues, adjust timing and coordinate the platform operator, camera operator and moderator. No one else changes the document during the broadcast.

faq.q: What tools keep the timeline visible to every owner?
faq.a: Asana or Monday.com for the master plan with dependencies; Google Docs or Notion for the living run of show; Zoom Events, Cvent or Bizzabo for the event layer; Eventbrite or Cvent for registration; HubSpot or Salesforce for post-event lead handoff.

faq.q: When do I need a backup stream versus a backup recording?
faq.a: A backup stream runs simultaneously on a second encoder and CDN so the live audience never sees a drop. A backup recording is a local capture for editing if the primary cloud recording fails. Hybrid events need both; webinars can often rely on the platform cloud recording alone.

faq.q: How does West Peek Productions fit into the timeline?
faq.a: West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations. It works on the platform you choose, supplies the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream, and can help you choose the platform if needed.
